newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P assigns counterparty ratings to Bank Niaga.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns counterparty ratings to Bank Niaga.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it had assigned BB long-term and B short-term foreign and local currency counterparty ratings to PT Bank Niaga.
S&P said in a statement that the ratings reflected the positive factors of the bank's acceptable asset quality, adequate provisioning, prudent management, profitability and capitalisation.
However, offsetting features were the bank's limited market share and small absolute capital and perceived high industry risks associated with the Indonesian banking sector, it said.

Bank Niaga, with unaudited assets of Indonesian rupiah 6.81 trillion (US$2.91 billion) at June 30, 1996, is Indonesia's 13th largest bank with a 1.6 percent of market share of Indonesia's commerical banking assets at the end of 1995, it said.

But the bank's capital base at June 30, 1996, of only US$206 million was small on an international basis, limiting the bank's flexibility to withstand potential losses from unanticipated events and the bank's absolute capital size is one of the lowest among Indonesia's largest 15 banks, S&P said.
The rating outlook is stable, the rating agency said, adding that it expected Bank Niaga's reasonable financial profile to continue into the medium term.
